tagline: Around the Bayfield Peninsula, harbor to harbor, apples on the hills.
intro: From a roundabout outside Ashland, WIS 13 follows Chequamegon Bay to Washburn, a brownstone boomtown, then runs north through open fields and pine to Bayfield, where the Apostle Islands come into view on the long hill into town. Past Red Cliff the road turns west along the top of the peninsula, drops steeply into Cornucopia and goes on by Herbster and Port Wing, crossing ravines at four or five to the mile, to the Brule River.

Lake Superior averages about 40 degrees and seldom freezes, which keeps the hills above Bayfield fit for apples and berries. The Apple Festival in October brings in tens of thousands. Bayfield, the smallest city in Wisconsin, has 584 people.

moments.title: Bayfield
moments.text: From the marina a ferry crosses to Madeline Island, the one Apostle left out of the national lakeshore, and the visitor center keeps an actual lighthouse light to stand beside.

moments.title: Mawikwe Bay sea caves
moments.text: Down Meyers Road, kayakers in summer and hikers in winter set out from the beach for the sea caves, and a trail runs along the top of the red sandstone cliffs.

moments.title: Cornucopia
moments.text: Wisconsin's northernmost town, reached by a steep descent, where an artesian well runs cold off the beach all year and Ehlers General Store has been open a hundred years.

practical: There is a fee to park at Meyers Beach.
